lines.trans: Patriots, I am missing both legs.
I have a broken pelvis.
I have a compromised lung.
But I came here to defend and say that all the blame for this belonged to the red one.
But this will not go unpunished.
Next Sunday we will be there.
In front of the eastern military command, protesting.
I will just need someone, of course.
Helping over there to push the patriot's wheelchair.

meanings.note: Person who claims devotion to their country.

examples.trans: Patriots, I am here to defend!

examples.text: Ajude a empurrar a cadeira do patriota.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Indicates lack or absence.
Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Masculine cardinal numeral (feminine duas).

examples.trans: She is looking for two bedrooms.

meanings.note: Lower limb of the human body.
Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: Anatomically refers to the hip bone or pelvis.

examples.text: Ele machucou a bacia na queda.
examples.trans: He hurt his pelvis in the fall.

meanings.note: Fractured or out of order.
Organ of respiration.

examples.text: Respire fundo para encher o pulmão.
examples.trans: Breathe deeply to fill your lungs.

meanings.note: Damaged or committed.
Introduces a contrast. The informal thanks softens the refusal; it does not accept the invitation.

examples.trans: It’s a meeting, but I’m not going.

meanings.note: Irregular verb: present ele vem (he comes), completed past ela veio (she came).

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.

meanings.note: Points to the speaker's location or reinforces demonstratives like isso aqui and esse slide aqui.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Vim aqui defender a nossa posição.
examples.trans: I came here to defend our position.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Covers speaking, talking, and telling in everyday Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: Responsibility for a mistake or disaster.

examples.text: A culpa toda disso foi dele.
examples.trans: All the blame for this was his.
I am not to blame for the delay.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number; before an adjective (todo travado) means completely.

examples.text: A culpa toda disso foi dele.
examples.trans: All the blame for this was his.
I am all locked up in my neck.

meanings.note: Neutral contraction of de + isso, referring to a whole situation rather than a gendered noun.

examples.trans: I want to know the reason for this.

meanings.note: Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Color of rubies or danger wires; also associated with left-wing politics.

examples.trans: Our wiring will never be red!

meanings.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun pointing to what was just said or done.
A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.
Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
Passar impune means to go unpunished; passar por means to undergo.

examples.text: Eles passam por muitos testes lá.
examples.trans: They go through many tests there.

meanings.note: Passar impune means to go unpunished.

examples.trans: The mistake did not go unpunished.

meanings.note: Domingo que vem means next Sunday.

examples.trans: Next Sunday we will be there.

meanings.note: Points to a place away from the speaker; lá dentro reinforces inside there.
Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.
Used in na frente de (in front of someone).

examples.text: Não grita na frente dos outros!
examples.trans: Don't shout in front of everyone else!

examples.text: Te espero na frente da sala.
examples.trans: I'll wait for you in front of the room.

meanings.note: Links verbs like faltar to an event or destination.
Military headquarters or control authority.

examples.text: Estaremos em frente ao comando militar.
examples.trans: We will be in front of the military command.

examples.text: Ele assumiu o comando da equipe.
examples.trans: He took command of the team.

meanings.note: Relating to the armed forces.

examples.text: Estaremos em frente ao comando militar.
examples.trans: We will be in front of the military command.

meanings.note: The eastern cardinal direction.

examples.text: Fica no comando militar do leste.
examples.trans: It is at the eastern military command.
The wind blows from the east.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: We will be right out front, protesting.

meanings.note: Limits a statement (eu só quero) or forms só que (except that / the catch is).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

examples.text: Só que agora ela precisa de ajuda.

meanings.note: Takes de before a noun (precisa da ajuda) and links directly to an infinitive (precisava gritar).

examples.text: Ela precisa da ajuda do colega.

examples.trans: Did you need to shout at me?

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun referring to an unspecified person.

examples.text: Vou precisar de alguém para ajudar.
examples.trans: I will need someone to help.

meanings.note: Used standalone in speech to mean of course / obviously.

examples.trans: I will need help, of course.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for offering or asking for assistance.

examples.trans: I am going to help you.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Preciso de alguém para empurrar a cadeira.
examples.trans: I need someone to push the chair.
Push the door to open it.

examples.text: Preciso empurrar a cadeira de rodas.
examples.trans: I need to push the wheelchair.

examples.trans: The car wheel got a flat.

meanings.note: Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).
Time between midday and evening; boa tarde! greets or bids farewell in the afternoon.

examples.text: A reunião é hoje à tarde.
